items.title: Physics & Astrophysics Greats — Raman, Bose, Saha, Chandrasekhar
items.body:
## The physicists who put India on the map

- **C.V. Raman** — discovered the **Raman Effect** (inelastic scattering of light) on **28 Feb 1928**; won the **Nobel Prize in Physics (1930)**, the first Asian science Nobel; **Bharat Ratna 1954**. 28 February is **National Science Day**. He studied at Mrs A.V.N. College, **Visakhapatnam (AP)**.
- **S.N. Bose** — worked out the quantum statistics of photons; his collaboration with Einstein gave **Bose–Einstein statistics** and the **Bose–Einstein condensate**. The particle class **'boson'** is named after him.
- **Meghnad Saha** — gave the **Saha thermal ionization equation** (1920), foundational to modern astrophysics and stellar spectra; also worked on river-valley planning (Damodar).
- **S. Chandrasekhar** — derived the **Chandrasekhar limit (~1.44 solar masses)**, the maximum mass of a stable white dwarf; **Nobel Physics 1983**. He was **C.V. Raman's nephew**; NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory honours him.
- **J.C. Bose (Jagadish Chandra Bose)** — pioneer of **radio/microwave** research who demonstrated wireless communication **before Marconi's public demonstration**; invented the **crescograph** to measure plant growth/response; founded the **Bose Institute (1917)**, Kolkata.

| Scientist | Signature contribution | Top honour |
|---|---|---|
| C.V. Raman | Raman Effect | Nobel Physics 1930 |
| S.N. Bose | Bose–Einstein statistics | Boson named after him |
| Meghnad Saha | Ionization equation | FRS |
| S. Chandrasekhar | Chandrasekhar limit | Nobel Physics 1983 |
keyPoints: C.V. Raman discovered the Raman Effect (28 Feb 1928), won Nobel Physics 1930, and got the Bharat Ratna in 1954; 28 Feb is National Science Day.
S.N. Bose gave Bose–Einstein statistics; the 'boson' is named after him.
Meghnad Saha formulated the Saha thermal ionization equation, foundational to astrophysics.
S. Chandrasekhar gave the Chandrasekhar limit (~1.44 solar masses) and won the Nobel Physics prize in 1983.
Chandrasekhar was C.V. Raman's nephew.
J.C. Bose demonstrated wireless/microwave communication before Marconi, invented the crescograph, and founded the Bose Institute (1917).
items.mnemonic: Physics four = Raman, Bose, Saha, Chandrasekhar — 'Really Bright Stars Cluster'.

items.title: Institution Builders — Bhabha, Sarabhai, Bhatnagar, P.C. Ray
items.body:
## Scientists who built India's research base

- **Homi J. Bhabha** — **father of India's nuclear programme**; gave the **cascade theory** of cosmic-ray showers; founded **TIFR (1945)**, headed the **Atomic Energy Commission**, and conceived the **three-stage nuclear power programme**. BARC, Trombay is named after him.
- **Vikram Sarabhai** — **father of the Indian space programme**; founded the **Physical Research Laboratory (PRL), Ahmedabad (1947)** and **INCOSPAR**, which became **ISRO (1969)**.
- **S.S. Bhatnagar** — first Director-General of **CSIR**; built India's chain of national laboratories. The **Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize**, India's top science award for under-45 scientists, is named after him.
- **P.C. Ray** — pioneer of Indian chemistry; founded **Bengal Chemical & Pharmaceutical Works**; called the **father of the Indian pharmaceutical industry**; discovered stable mercurous nitrite.
- **C.N.R. Rao** — eminent **solid-state and materials chemist**; founded the **Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR)**, Bengaluru; awarded the **Bharat Ratna in 2014** (third scientist to receive it, after C.V. Raman and A.P.J. Abdul Kalam).

## Why they matter for the exam
These founders established the institutions (TIFR, PRL/ISRO, CSIR labs, JNCASR, indigenous pharma) that anchor India's S&T policy questions in Paper-II and Mains Paper-V.
keyPoints: Homi Bhabha: father of India's nuclear programme; founded TIFR; conceived the three-stage nuclear programme; BARC named after him.
Vikram Sarabhai: father of the Indian space programme; founded PRL Ahmedabad and INCOSPAR (forerunner of ISRO).
S.S. Bhatnagar: first DG of CSIR; the SSB Prize for scientists under 45 is named after him.
P.C. Ray: father of the Indian pharmaceutical industry; founded Bengal Chemical & Pharmaceutical Works.
C.N.R. Rao: solid-state/materials chemist, founded JNCASR, and received the Bharat Ratna in 2014.

items.title: Indian-origin Nobel & Global Laureates — Khorana, Ramakrishnan, Ramanujan
items.body:
## Global recognition

- **Har Gobind Khorana** — shared the **1968 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine** (with Nirenberg and Holley) for interpreting the **genetic code** and its role in protein synthesis; later achieved the first chemical synthesis of a gene.
- **Venkatraman Ramakrishnan** — shared the **2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry** (with Steitz and Yonath) for the atomic structure of the **ribosome**; later President of the Royal Society, London.
- **Srinivasa Ramanujan** — self-taught mathematical genius; landmark work in **number theory, infinite series, continued fractions and modular forms**; collaborated with **G.H. Hardy**; **FRS 1918**. His birthday, **22 December**, is **National Mathematics Day**.

## Nobel science laureates linked to India
| Laureate | Year | Field |
|---|---|---|
| C.V. Raman | 1930 | Physics |
| Har Gobind Khorana | 1968 | Medicine |
| S. Chandrasekhar | 1983 | Physics |
| Venkatraman Ramakrishnan | 2009 | Chemistry |
keyPoints: Har Gobind Khorana shared the 1968 Nobel (Medicine) for interpreting the genetic code.
Venkatraman Ramakrishnan shared the 2009 Nobel (Chemistry) for the ribosome structure.
Ramanujan's birthday (22 December) is National Mathematics Day; he worked with G.H. Hardy and was FRS in 1918.
Science Nobel laureates linked to India: Raman (1930), Khorana (1968), Chandrasekhar (1983), Ramakrishnan (2009).
items.mnemonic: Science Nobels timeline: Raman 1930 → Khorana 1968 → Chandrasekhar 1983 → Ramakrishnan 2009.

items.title: Applied Science for the Nation — Kalam, Swaminathan, Kurien
items.body:
## Science that transformed everyday India

- **A.P.J. Abdul Kalam** — 'Missile Man'; project director of **SLV-III** (India's first satellite launch vehicle, 1980); led the **IGMDP** (Agni, Prithvi); key to **Pokhran-II (1998)**; **President of India (2002–07)**; **Bharat Ratna 1997**.
- **M.S. Swaminathan** — **father of the Green Revolution** in India; introduced high-yielding wheat/rice varieties with Norman Borlaug; founded the **M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation**; **Bharat Ratna 2024 (posthumous)**.
- **Verghese Kurien** — **father of the White Revolution**; architect of **Operation Flood** (world's largest dairy programme), the **Amul** cooperative model and the **NDDB**; made India the world's largest milk producer.

## Mains angle
These figures show how S&T translated into **food, milk and defence self-reliance** — a ready 'science for national development / Atmanirbhar Bharat' example for Paper-V.
keyPoints: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam directed SLV-III and the IGMDP missiles, was central to Pokhran-II (1998), President 2002–07, Bharat Ratna 1997.
M.S. Swaminathan is the father of India's Green Revolution; Bharat Ratna 2024 (posthumous).
Verghese Kurien is the father of the White Revolution; led Operation Flood, Amul and the NDDB.
Together they anchor a 'science for national self-reliance' argument in Mains Paper-V.
items.mnemonic: Three revolutions of self-reliance: Kalam (defence/space), Swaminathan (Green/food), Kurien (White/milk).

items.title: Andhra Connection & Contemporary Women Scientists
items.body:
## Andhra Pradesh's own

- **Yellapragada Subbarao** — born **12 January 1895 at Bhimavaram (West Godavari, AP)**; biochemist who synthesised **folic acid**, developed the anti-cancer drug **methotrexate**, discovered **diethylcarbamazine (DEC)** for filariasis, and uncovered the role of **ATP** in muscular energy. Largely unrecognised in his lifetime; worked at Lederle Laboratories, USA.
- **C.V. Raman's AP link** — studied at **Mrs A.V.N. College, Visakhapatnam** before Presidency College.

## Contemporary women scientists

- **Tessy Thomas** — DRDO's 'Missile Woman'; Project Director of the **Agni-IV/V** missiles.
- **Ritu Karidhal** — ISRO's 'Rocket Woman'; mission-director roles in **Mangalyaan** and **Chandrayaan** missions.
- **Nigar Shaji** — Project Director of the **Aditya-L1** solar mission (launched Sep 2023).

| Scientist | Organisation | Known for |
|---|---|---|
| Y. Subbarao | Lederle (USA) | Folic acid, methotrexate, DEC |
| Tessy Thomas | DRDO | Agni missiles |
| Ritu Karidhal | ISRO | Mars/Moon missions |
| Nigar Shaji | ISRO | Aditya-L1 |
keyPoints: Yellapragada Subbarao (born Bhimavaram, AP) synthesised folic acid and methotrexate and discovered diethylcarbamazine for filariasis.
C.V. Raman studied at Mrs A.V.N. College, Visakhapatnam.
Tessy Thomas ('Missile Woman') was Project Director of the Agni missiles at DRDO.
Ritu Karidhal ('Rocket Woman') held mission-director roles in Mangalyaan and Chandrayaan.
Nigar Shaji was Project Director of ISRO's Aditya-L1 solar mission (2023).
items.mnemonic: AP biochemist Subbarao = 'Folic-Metho-DEC-ATP' — four life-saving discoveries.
